**Visual observations:**
- Soybean seedling collapsed at soil level
- Stem/hypocotyl shows dark necrotic lesion right at the soil line
- Leaves are brown, wilted, and papery dead
- Sandy/dry soil
- Adjacent healthy plants visible
- Classic "post-emergence damping-off" symptom pattern

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Pythium_damping_off**: Causes seedling collapse at soil line, soft water-soaked rot, pre/post-emergence death. Classic symptom is exactly this — seedling stands then collapses suddenly.
- **Rhizoctonia**: Also causes damping-off with reddish-brown sunken hypocotyl lesions, but lesion tends to be more defined and reddish.
- **Phytophthora**: Root/stem rot that typically affects larger plants; brown discoloration extends up the stem.
- **Fusarium**: Root rot but usually more gradual; infected plants often show yellowing before death.

The image shows a seedling in complete post-emergence collapse at soil level — the hallmark of damping-off. The stem appears to have failed right at the soil line. The dry sandy soil argues slightly against Pythium (which prefers wet conditions), but the symptom pattern — sudden seedling death, stem pinching at soil level — is most consistent with Pythium damping-off.
